 October 30, 2026 18:40 Sun Pharma Q2 profit declines 36% to Rs 1,989 cr
 Pharma major Sun Pharmaceutical Industries on Friday reported a 36.36 per cent decline in consolidated net profit at Rs 1,988.53 crore for the September quarter, dragged down by a one-time expenditure related to the proposed acquisition of Organon and litigation expenses in the US.
 The company had posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 3,124.95 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries said in a regulatory filing.
 Consolidated total revenue from operations in the second quarter of the current fiscal stood at Rs 16,198.71 crore as compared to Rs 14,478.31 crore in the year-ago period, it added.
 The rise in revenues was driven by an increase in formulation sales in India -- up 17.3 per cent to Rs 5,552.3 crore -- accounting for 34.5 per cent of the total consolidated sales for the quarter.
 Total expenses during the quarter under review were higher at Rs 12,287.83 crore as compared to Rs 10,780.62 crore a year ago, the company said. (PTI) 
 October 30, 2026 18:39 Motherson Sumi's Q2 profit grows 35% to Rs 223 crore
 Auto component major Motherson Sumi Wiring India Ltd on Friday posted 35 per cent growth in net profit at Rs 223.37 crore for September quarter FY27 as increased content per vehicle and orders for new models drove the company’s revenue higher.
 In the year-ago period, the company’s net profit was Rs 165.34 crore. EBITDA grew 33.6 per cent to Rs 374 crore. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 4,053.83 crore from Rs 2,761.86 crore, according to an exchange filing.
 EBITDA margin contracted to 9.2 per cent during the quarter from 10.1 per cent in the year-ago period. Total expenses during the quarter increased by 47.8 per cent to Rs 3,755.64 crore as cost of material consumed jumped 55 per cent to Rs 2,905.46 crore. (PTI) 
 October 30, 2026 18:25 Welspun Living Q2 net profit jumps multi-fold to Rs 169.66 cr, revenue rises 12.3%
 Home textiles major Welspun Living Ltd on Friday reported a multi-fold rise in its consolidated net profit to Rs 169.66 crore for the September quarter of FY27.
 The company had posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 14.86 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
 Its revenue from operations rose 12.3 per cent to Rs 2.838.12 crore in the second quarter of the current fiscal, compared to Rs 2,440.91 crore in the corresponding period a year ago.
 Total expenses of Welspun Living stood at Rs 2,636.77 crore, up 8.42 per cent year-on-year.
 Its revenue from the Home Textiles segment increased 15.82 per cent to Rs 2,689.02 crore.
 Similarly, its ‘Flooring’ business was also up 19.3 per cent at Rs 216.23 crore.
 Total income rose 16.86 per cent to Rs 2,869.90 crore in the quarter under review.
 In the first half (H1) of FY27, total consolidated income from operations of Welspun Living stood at Rs 5,698 crore, up 20.21 per cent year-on-year. (PTI) 
 October 30, 2026 18:14 Zee Entertainment Q2 profit drops 40.4% to Rs 45.6 cr, revenue up at Rs 2,247 cr
 Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd on Friday reported a 40.4 per cent year-on-year decline in its consolidated net profit to Rs 45.6 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on account of higher advertising and promotional spends and impact on advertising revenue.
 It had posted a net profit of Rs 76.5 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
 However, its total income jumped 12.6 per cent to Rs 2.247.2 crore in Q2 FY27, from Rs 1,995.6 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal.
 The revenue growth was “driven by Digital Business”, said Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd in its earnings presentation.
 ZEEL’s total expenses stood at Rs 2,184.1 crore, up 16.15 per cent YoY, compared to Rs 1,880.3 crore in the second quarter of FY26. (PTI) 
 October 30, 2026 18:12 Bank of Baroda posts record high profit of Rs 6,532 crore in Q2
 Bank of Baroda on Friday reported its highest-ever quarterly net profit of Rs 6,532 crore, registering a growth of 35.8 per cent in the second quarter of 2026-27 financial year.
 Its profit was Rs 4,809.39 crore in the July-September period of 2025-26. The bank’s net interest income (NII) in the quarter under review expanded by 9 per cent to Rs 13,026 crore, according to a stock exchange filing.
 The lender’s domestic advances were at Rs 11,87,944 crore, a growth of 13.5 per cent year-on-year, while global advances were Rs 15,12,448 crore, growing by 18.3 per cent.
 The bank further said its domestic deposits increased by 16.6 per cent to Rs 14,83,521 crore in September this year.
 Global deposits too grew 16.4 per cent to Rs 17,45,435 crore. Gross NPA ratio improved to 1.78 per cent in Q2FY27 from 2.16 per cent in Q2FY26. (PTI) 
 October 30, 2026 18:09 GE Vernova T&D India profit up 44% to Rs 431 cr in Q2

 The net profit was Rs 299.48 crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2025, an exchange filing said.
 Total income rose to Rs 2,077.31 crore in the quarter from Rs 1,557.09 crore in the same period a year ago. (PTI)

 October 30, 2026 18:05 Unimech Aerospace Q2 FY27 Revenue Rises 98% YoY to Rs. 1,230 Mn; EBITDA Grows 164%, and PAT 103%
 Unimech Aerospace & Manufacturing Ltd., a global high precision engineering platform specializing in manufacturing complex products, announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026.
 Revenue stood at Rs. 1,230.0 Mn, registering a strong 98% YoY and 14% QoQ growth supported by healthy demand and robust execution.
 • H1 FY27 Revenue stood at Rs.2,306.2 Mn, achieving ~96% of FY26 Revenues
 • EBITDA in Q2 stood at Rs.490.1 Mn up 164% YoY with robust margins of 40% and for H1 stood at Rs.882.6 Mn up 130% YoY highlighting operational excellence, a high-margin order mix, and strong operating leverage
 • PAT in Q2 stood at Rs. 317.7 Mn, up 103% YoY and for H1 at Rs. 596.4 Mn, up 71% YoY capping a strong quarter of profitable growth and reinforcing our confidence in the momentum ahead. (PTI) 
 October 30, 2026 18:03 Indian Oil's Q2 profit nearly triples on LPG compensation
 Indian Oil Corporation reported a nearly threefold jump in second-quarter profit on Friday, helped by government compensation for ‌domestic LPG losses despite higher crude prices.
 The state-run company’s standalone net profit rose to 216.30 billion rupees ($2.28 ‌billion) in the quarter ended September 30, from 76.10 billion rupees ‌a year earlier
 * Revenue from ‌operations ⁠rose about 30% to ⁠2.63 trillion rupees, helped by 72.43 billion rupees received from the federal government as compensation for under-recoveries incurred on domestic LPG ‌sales during April-September
 * Under-recoveries are losses incurred by state-run fuel retailers on subsidized LPG sales, which the government reimburses ‌periodically through compensation payments. (Reuters)
 October 30, 2026 18:00 Trent shares jump over 5% after strong Q2 results; m-cap rises by Rs 7,950 cr
 Shares of Tata Group’s retail arm Trent Ltd on Friday ended over 5 per cent higher after the firm reported a 25 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter.
 The stock climbed 5.20 per cent to settle at Rs 3,015.10 on the BSE. During the day, it surged 6.73 per cent to a high of Rs 3,059.
 At the NSE, the stock jumped 5.43 per cent to end at Rs 3,017.30.
 The company’s market valuation increased by Rs 7,950.47 crore to Rs 1,60,774.84 crore.
 The stock was the biggest gainer among the Sensex and Nifty firms.
 Trent Ltd on Thursday reported a 25 per cent YoY increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 468 crore for the September quarter, as revenue growth and operating leverage supported earnings amid an inflationary environment.
 Consolidated revenue from operations rose 22 per cent to Rs 5,873 crore in the quarter ended September 30, while operating earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) increased 37 per cent to Rs 785 crore, the company said in a statement on Thursday. (PTI)

 Smartworks Q2 results live: Management commentary
 Smartworks Founder and Managing Director Neetish Sarda said the company delivered a strong first-half performance and was tracking ahead of its FY27 plan. He highlighted 39 per cent revenue growth and more than doubling of normalised profit after tax in Q2 FY27, prompting the company to raise its full-year revenue growth guidance. He attributed the growth to sustained demand from existing clients, new global businesses, Indian conglomerates and GCCs, adding that Smartworks had recorded six consecutive quarters of sequential revenue and margin growth, with margins expanding around 360 basis points.

 Q2 FY27 Performance Overview
 • Revenue from operations: ₹591 crore, up 39% year-on-year and 8% QoQ.
 • Revenue from GCC clients contributes ~22% of rental revenue.
 • Normalised EBITDA: ₹117 crore, up 68% year-on-year, with margins improving to 19.8% from16.4% a year ago.
 • Normalised profit after tax: ₹43.4 crore, up 136% year-on-year.
 • Normalised operating cash flow: ₹107 crore, up 74% year-on-year.
 • Annualised normalised ROCE: 21.6%, compared with 13.6% a year ago.
 • Contracted rental revenue: ~ ₹5,800 crore, providing strong visibility into future revenue.

 AEQUS Q2 RESULTS LIVE:
 AEQUS Q2FY27 Concall - Nuvama:
 Overall
 - Aerospace = 86% of Q2 revenue, main growth driver. Consumer revenue 2x in H1 but slower than expected.
 - Q2 EBITDA: Rs 245mn, 6% margin vs 16% in Q2FY26 - hit by consumer losses, higher employee/subcon cost, adverse aerospace mix.
 Aerospace - Strong
 - H1 Revenue +42% YoY, EBITDA +29% YoY.
 - Order book at $1.1bn, +9% QoQ - visibility for 5-7 years, some contracts up to 15 years.
 - New: Long-term deal with 6 Safran entities - for engine & landing gear parts. Commercialization from FY29 at new Hosur plant.
 - Capacity Utilization: 69% overall, 76% in India (+8pp YoY). Added 9 CMC machines (Total 229), Added 238 new parts (Total 5,978 parts).
 - Titanium: Used in 1000+ parts (A320neo, B787). Aequs is one of India’s largest buyers. Cost is pass-through, no pricing pressure.
 - Inventory build-up is intentional - to support growth. To normalize by Q1FY28, target 120 days.
 Consumer Electronics - Weak
 - Utilization down: 22% (Q1) to 17% (Q2).
 - Reason: Longer re-qualification after product updates, process mods, supply chain issues.
 - Fixed cost heavy - low volume = high losses.
 - Breakeven at ∼50% utilization. Earlier target of Q4FY27 EBITDA breakeven is now delayed - no new timeline. PAT positive target still FY30.
 Toys - Transition
 - Q2 was transition quarter. Old customer phasing out in Q3, new key customer ramping up.
 - Hit by component delays and logistics. Expected to focus fully on new customer by Q4FY27.
 Capex & Funding
 - H1 Capex: Rs 1.59bn. FY27 full year guidance cut from Rs 6.6bn to ~Rs 3.2bn (H2 similar to H1).
 - Focus shift: More money to Aerospace (Hosur), less to Consumer till utilization improves.
 - Promoter infusion: Rs 6.5bn via warrants - Rs 2.89bn for capex, Rs 1bn WC, Rs 1bn for JV.
 - Plus Rs 8bn term loan planned. May need another raise in FY28.
 - Net Debt/Equity up to 0.5x from 0.2x in FY26. Borrowings up Rs 1.58bn in H1.
 Guidance
 - Aerospace on track for FY27. Long-term target 4-6x growth by FY31 retained.
 - Consumer breakeven timeline under recalibration.
 - New CFO: Reena Joseph joined.
